explanation: Compared against WOWII conjecture 33 (Wayback copy of all.html and wowIIdefs.js): for simple connected G, path(G) ≥ CEIL[2·distavg(M,V)]. Here path(G) is the number of vertices of a largest induced path (def 35), distavg(M,V) is the average of all nonzero dist(u,v) with u of maximum degree and v ∈ V (def 37), and CEIL is the ceiling (def 16). The source records an Oct 2005 counterexample (path 7, distavg 3.56). The Lean statement negates the universal claim over connected, nontrivial finite graphs. `path` uses isInducedPath (adjacency iff consecutive), and distAvg averages over (m, v) ∈ M × V with nonzero distance. That matches the definitions. Faithful.
